extracted.intended_audience: senior researchers considering applying for a Royal Society Research Professorship (UK/relocating to UK)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility/assessment criteria for applicants to the Royal Society Research Professorship scheme (senior, world-class researchers seeking long-term funding and/or relocation to the UK). Covers who is eligible, what materials are required at each stage, allowable costs, and selection procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: World-class researcher of outstanding achievement and promise
rubrics_metrics.description: This scheme is for you if: You are a world-class researcher of outstanding achievement and promise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are expected to be internationally leading researchers whose track record demonstrates outstanding achievement and promise. The scheme is designed to enable such researchers to focus on ambitious and original research of the highest quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: prevented from full research capability by competing duties (UK-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible if currently prevented from achieving full research capability by competing duties (i.e. already based in the UK).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants in this category should demonstrate how competing duties limit their current research capacity and how the Professorship would enable full research capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: wish to relocate to the UK to undertake research
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible if you are a world-class researcher who wishes to relocate to the UK to undertake their research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications from internationally renowned researchers residing outside the UK are particularly welcomed; relocation and visa costs can be requested and the scheme supports Global Talent Visa fast-track endorsement for eligible candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research within Royal Society remit (natural sciences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your research must be within the Royal Society’s remit of natural sciences, which includes but is not limited to biological research and biomedical sciences, chemistry, engineering, mathematics and physics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult the full 'breakdown of subject groups and areas' supported by the Royal Society to confirm fit. Proposals outside this remit are not appropriate for the scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nationality and visa eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The scheme is open to applicants of all nationalities; applications are particularly welcomed from internationally renowned researchers currently residing outside of the UK.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Royal Society Research Professors requiring a visa to work in the UK are eligible for the Global Talent Visa under the fast-track endorsement process; applicants should ensure visa eligibility and include relocation/visa costs where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-stage application and selection process
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are processed through a two-stage selection process: Stage 1 (CV and lay summary) and Stage 2 (full application for invited applicants). Shortlisted applicants will be invited to attend an interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage 1 requires submission of CV and lay summary; Stage 1 applications are assessed by the Royal Society Research Professorships Panel. Only invited applicants submit full Stage 2 applications. Read scheme notes for further details on each stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 required materials: CV and lay summary
rubrics_metrics.description: The first stage will involve the submission of the applicant's CV and a lay summary of their proposed research. These applications will be assessed by the Royal Society Research Professorships Panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lay summary should clearly communicate the proposed research at a non-specialist level. The panel uses these materials to decide who is invited to Stage 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview process and feedback sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: For candidates shortlisted for an interview, the Society will share points raised by reviewers in advance which should be addressed during the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shortlisted candidates should prepare to respond to reviewer comments. The practice of sharing reviewer points is intended to make interviews focused and allow applicants to address specific concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award duration and maximum funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Professors are appointed for up to ten years and funding can be requested up to £3 million to cover this period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should prepare proposals and costs for a ten-year fellowship. Note scheme change from previous five-year model; costs for years 6–10 are conditional on satisfactory progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional funding for years 6–10 (mid-fellowship checkpoint)
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs for years six to ten will be subject to satisfactory progress and completion of a mid-fellowship checkpoint review in year four.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding for the later half of the fellowship is not unconditional; applicants should plan deliverables/milestones and be prepared for a formal checkpoint in year four.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable costs and budget items
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds can cover: a contribution to the award holder's basic salary of up to £90,000 per annum; indirect and estate costs; equipment costs and research expenses including consumables, travel, etc; contribution towards research assistance salary and associated indirect and estate costs; support for a new four-year PhD studentship(s); relocation and visa costs for the applicant and their dependents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The total grant cap may be exceeded to cover relocation/visa costs if well justified. Include detailed justification for high-cost items and show how each budget line supports the research objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision for personal circumstances and flexible working
rubrics_metrics.description: The Society provides flexibility to accommodate personal circumstances including part-time working, sabbaticals and secondments. There is provision for maternity, paternity, shared parental, adoptive or extended sick leave, as well as financial support for childcare costs that arise from attending conferences and research visits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should describe any planned part-time working or career breaks and how these will be managed. The scheme explicitly allows such arrangements and financial support for associated costs where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for disabled applicants and reasonable adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Royal Society welcomes applications from disabled applicants and provides support and adjustments to ensure full participation in the selection process. Adjustments can include deadline extensions, support to complete the application form, alternative formats, interview support including technical accessibility, and additional costs to attend interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for adjustments are confidential and not normally shared with panel members unless necessary; if sharing is required the Society will ask permission. Contact details (seniorfellowships@royalsociety.org) are provided for arranging adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity, diversity and inclusion (EDI) commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Royal Society recognises that diversity is essential for excellence in STEM and wants to encourage applications from the widest range of backgrounds; policies and processes are reviewed to embed EDI principles in grant making and ensure all talented applicants have an equitable chance to succeed as per the assessment criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants from underrepresented backgrounds are encouraged to apply. Panels and processes are intended to account for EDI; applicants can expect EDI to be considered alongside scientific assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum number of awards
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be up to two awards available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware of limited award numbers when assessing competitiveness of the scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission system requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You will apply through our application and grant management system, Flexi-Grant®.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All applications must be submitted via Flexi-Grant®; follow the system's instructions and use the scheme notes for system-specific guidance.
